neighbours.label: A substance taken for its effect on the body has just been named: alcohol, tobacco or medicine
fire: After the funeral, the brothers sat on the steps and passed around a bottle of whiskey.
Grandpa kept a tin of pipe tobacco on the shelf beside his chair.
My doctor told me to stop the antibiotics if the rash got worse.
By midnight the whole crew was drunk on cheap wine and singing.
With the headache getting worse, she chewed two aspirin dry.
The old sailor stuffed his cheek with snuff and spat over the rail.
Patients who miss a dose of insulin should call the clinic right away.
At the tavern he ordered a pint of ale and a glass of brandy.
quiet: Once the service ended, the cousins stood in the yard and looked through old photographs.
Grandma stored a box of brass buttons in the drawer under her sewing machine.
The physio said to stop running if the knee got worse.
Late that night the tired crew was mending nets and humming.
With the deadline getting closer, she folded two letters neatly.
The young deckhand tied his boots with tarred rope and looked out to sea.
Anyone who misses an appointment should phone the front desk right away.
At the hardware store he bought a pound of nails and a box of screws.

notes: Top examples list tobacco, meds, beer and dose. Probing: rum, pipe, pills and meds fired, plain milk much less, so the shared pattern is taken for effect, not food in general.
